original_title: Development of Hydrophobic Tag Based HDAC6 Degrader for Ulcerative Colitis Treatment
title: A hydrophobic-tag HDAC6 degrader aimed at ulcerative colitis
blurb: Built off Nexturastat A, this series hauls HDAC6 to the proteasome via hydrophobic tagging rather than a PROTAC-style ternary complex. Lead compound 20c selectively degrades HDAC6 in vitro at a DC50 of 1.1 uM through the ubiquitin-proteasome system, though that's cell data, not a colitis model yet.

original_title: K2S2O8–Promoted C3-Bromination of Heteroarenes with Sodium Bromide
title: A cheap bromination route for heteroarene C3 positions
blurb: K2S2O8 and sodium bromide, no exotic brominating agent, delivering C3-brominated quinoxalinones, cinnolinones, coumarins, and oxazinones across 38 examples in moderate to good yields. Works on late-stage pharmaceutical intermediates and scales to grams, with TFA apparently doing crucial mechanistic work.

original_title: Directing Group Migration Strategy: Ru(II)-Catalyzed Domino C–H Functionalization toward the Synthesis of 1,4-Dihydroisoquinolin-3(2 H )-One Scaffolds
title: A directing group that migrates before it gets to work
blurb: Ru(II)-catalyzed domino C–H functionalization where the directing group walks itself to a new position mid-sequence, then a 1,6-aza-conjugate addition between N-carbamoyl indoles and alkynylated p-quinone methides closes out 1,4-dihydroisoquinolin-3(2H)-one bisheterocycles. Broad substrate scope, good-to-excellent yields, and it tolerates late-stage functionalization.

original_title: Recent Advances and Future Directions in On-DNA Reaction Development
title: DEL chemistry finally gets some new reactions to play with
blurb: A review tracking on-DNA reaction development past the old mild-aqueous playbook that kept DNA-encoded libraries structurally boring. Photochemistry, electrochemistry, biocatalysis, and complexity-generating reactions are widening what you can actually build on a DNA tag, and that accessible chemical space is basically the whole point of DEL.

original_title: Synthesis of the Pentacyclic Skeleton of Cortistatins
title: 13 steps into the cortistatin skeleton
blurb: A concise route to the pentacyclic core of cortistatins: a [5+2] cycloaddition builds the oxabicyclo[3.2.1]octene B/C rings, then a Pauson-Khand reaction closes the D/E ring while installing the carbonyl and isoquinoline side chain in one shot. Two structural problems solved by one reaction.

original_title: Expanding the Repertoire of Lysosomal Degradation of Membrane Proteins: A Generalizable Strategy Using Multivalent Antibody−Polymer Chimeras
title: Degrading membrane proteins without borrowing a real lysosome receptor
blurb: Multivalent antibody-polymer chimeras drag a target membrane protein into the lysosome by pairing it with an ancillary membrane protein, and that ancillary partner doesn't need any native lysosome-targeting ability of its own, just enough multivalent noncovalent engagement to trigger endosomal uptake. Widens which proteins are degradable beyond the usual receptor-dependent tricks, assuming it generalizes past whatever targets they tested.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Modern Higher-Order Cycloadditions
title: Everything past the Diels-Alder
blurb: A review of higher-order cycloadditions, the pericyclic reactions running on more than 6π electrons, covering the 8π-18π range and how metal-, Lewis acid-, organo-, and enzyme-catalyzed versions each handle building bigger polycyclic frameworks than a plain Diels-Alder can reach.

original_title: Organocatalytic Cascade Aza-Mannich/Michael Addition Sequence for the Synthesis of Chiral ε-Sultam Derivatives
title: Chiral sultams via a Mannich then Michael
blurb: A bifunctional H-bonding organocatalyst runs [3+2] and [4+2] annulations between aminoenones and seven-membered cyclic N-sulfonylimines to build ε-sultams, with dr up to >20:1 and er up to 99:1. They also ran it gram-scale and pushed the products through further transformations, so it's more than a small-scale proof of concept.

original_title: Benchmarking Hydrogen and Oxygen Electrocatalytic Reactions in Acidic and Alkaline Media on Iridium Single-Crystal Surfaces
title: Iridium single crystals get the benchmarking treatment
blurb: HER, HOR, ORR, and hydrogen peroxide reduction measured on Ir(111), Ir(100), and Ir(110) in both acid and base. Iridium is the metal everyone leans on for energy conversion but rarely studies as a clean metallic surface, so this fills in a baseline that arguably should've existed already.

original_title: A carrier-within-a-carrier system with calcium nanoparticles encapsulated in β-cyclodextrin-polysaccharide hydrogel for verteporfin delivery and radiosensitization in orthotopic osteosarcoma.
title: A carrier inside a carrier, for verteporfin
blurb: Calcium nanoparticles packed into a β-cyclodextrin-polysaccharide hydrogel, built to deliver verteporfin and boost radiosensitization in orthotopic osteosarcoma. Double encapsulation as the delivery trick here.

original_title: Photocatalytic Activation of Fluoroform for Radical Trifluoromethylation
title: Getting a real CF3 radical out of fluoroform
blurb: Fluoroform is the cheap, low-toxicity trifluoromethyl source everyone wants to use, but it's mostly only handed over CF3 anions or metal-bound species, not the radical needed for radical trifluoromethylation. This method gets there photocatalytically by leveraging ketone reactivity, opening fluoroform up for the radical routes that matter most in medicinal chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Node-Assisted Photoredox Reactivity Enables MOF-Catalyzed Hydrogen/Deuterium Exchange in Aromatic Aldehydes
title: MOFs take over H/D exchange from the thiol catalysts
blurb: UiO-66-type MOFs run node-assisted photoredox H/D exchange on aromatic aldehydes without the usual thiol HAT catalyst, and selectively at the formyl position. Isotopic labeling has been a homogeneous-catalysis game for a while, so a thiol-free, formyl-selective heterogeneous platform is a genuine gap being filled, not just another catalyst variant.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Activity Delivery and Radiation Exposure in (177)Lu-Based Therapies: Prospective Evaluation of a Single-Puncture Closed System with Programmable Infusion.
title: A closed-system rig for dosing Lu-177 with one needle stick instead of several
blurb: Prospective evaluation of a single-puncture closed system with programmable infusion for delivering Lu-177 radiopharmaceutical therapies, tracking both how much activity actually reaches the patient and how much radiation the staff eat along the way. Unglamorous plumbing paper, but it's exactly this kind of workflow detail that decides whether a PRRT suite cuts its exposure numbers.

original_title: Alternating Copolymerization of Cyclobutenes and Norbornenes by a Dual-Site Grubbs Catalyst
title: A Grubbs catalyst that forces cyclobutene and norbornene to alternate instead of homopolymerizing
blurb: Alternating copolymerization usually cheats by picking monomers too reluctant to homopolymerize on their own. This uses a sterically bulky, dual-site chiral Grubbs catalyst to force strict alternation between cyclobutenes and norbornenes, both of which are perfectly happy polymerizing with themselves given the chance. That's the hard version of this reaction, not the usual rigged one.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Successive Ring Expansion Strategies for the Synthesis of Macrocycles and Medium-Sized Rings
title: Growing macrocycles by expanding rings twice instead of stitching them end to end
blurb: A review of strategies that chain two or more ring-expansion steps in sequence to reach macrocycles and medium-sized rings, sidestepping the inefficient end-to-end cyclizations these targets usually demand. A route map for the synthetic toolbox, not new chemistry itself.

original_title: Synthesis and Structures of Novel Chiral Cyclic Hypervalent Iodine(III) Reagents for Metal‐Free Ligand‐Transfer Reactions
title: New chiral hypervalent iodine(III) reagents for ligand transfer with no metal involved
blurb: A set of chiral λ3-iodane reagents for metal-free ligand transfer, including the first chiral bis(cyano-λ3-iodane) and the first chiral benziodoxolones carrying a carbon-based ligand, cyano or trifluoromethyl, next to a lactate group. Mostly a structural report for now, but if the transfer chemistry performs, it's a metal-free route into asymmetric halogenation and cyanation.

original_title: Chirality-Matched Cyclopropenimine–Thiourea Organocatalysis for Regiocontrolled Ring-Opening Polymerization of Methyl Glycolide
title: Regiocontrolled PLGA synthesis without a metal catalyst in sight
blurb: Methyl glycolide has two ring-opening sites of nearly identical reactivity, which is why precise alternating PLGA has been hard to hit. Pairing a cyclopropenimine base with a thiourea in a chirality-matched setup steers the ring-opening polymerization regioselectively, without the metal residues that dog the organometallic versions used in this biomedical polymer.

original_title: Visible-Light-Assisted Chemoselective Hydrogenation of Arylalkenes and Arylalkynes Using Water as the Hydrogen Source
title: Hydrogenating alkenes and alkynes with water as the hydrogen source, just blue light and no metal
blurb: PPh3 and I2 form a halogen-bonding complex under blue light that pulls hydrogen out of water for chemoselective hydrogenation of arylalkenes and arylalkynes, running through polar hydroiodination and then a phosphine radical cation strips the iodine back off. Good yields, tolerates aryl and nonbenzylic alkyl iodides, and no metal catalyst anywhere. Water as the actual reductant is the part worth noting.

original_title: Systematic Tuning of Lattice Strain and Surface Structures of Platinum Alloy Nanowires for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Performance
title: Dialing Pt alloy nanowires from smooth to nanobumpy for better oxygen reduction
blurb: Systematically tuned the morphology of Pt-alloy nanowires and found the nanobumpy Pt70Ni28Co1W1 wire on carbon wins out, posting 1.6 A/mg-Pt mass activity and 3.9 mA/cm²-Pt specific activity for oxygen reduction. Real numbers on a fuel-cell-relevant metric, from a systematic strain and surface-structure sweep rather than a lucky single sample.

original_title: Disentangling Structural and Electronic Roles of Pyridinic- and Pyrrolic-N in Ni-Catalyzed Hydrogenolysis of Aryl Ether Bonds
title: Sorting out which flavor of nitrogen actually helps Ni cleave aryl ethers
blurb: Nitrogen-doped carbon supports for Ni hydrogenolysis catalysts usually get credited to nitrogen doping in general, so this pulls pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N apart to see which handles the structural work and which the electronic. The optimized Ni/NC35 catalyst hits complete conversion on diphenyl ether, the standard lignin-relevant model for aryl ether C–O cleavage.

original_title: Advances in Catalytic Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkenes
title: Internal alkenes are the annoying substrate in hydrosilylation, and here's where the field stands
blurb: A review rounding up recent hydrosilylation methods aimed specifically at internal alkenes, the class that's always been trouble thanks to thermodynamic stability, steric crowding, and poor regiocontrol. Organized by substrate type, ring-strained through unactivated dialkyl, so it's a map of what works where rather than one new method.

original_title: Domino Route toward 1,5-Diazocines from 1,4,5,6-Tetrahydropyrimidines and Propiolic Acid Derivatives via a Ring Expansion Strategy
title: Building eight-membered diazocine rings in one pot from six-membered starting material
blurb: Tetrahydropyrimidines plus propiolic esters or amides form an enyne adduct that, kicked by acid or acid chloride, runs an aza-Claisen rearrangement paired with a formal enyne metathesis to expand the ring straight from six-membered to the eight-membered 1,5-diazocine. One pot, ambient conditions, 39-80% yield over the sequence, respectable for a medium ring that usually needs far more babying.

original_title: Ru-Catalyzed Deoxygenative Aromatization of Succinimides and Oxindoles to Pyrroles and Indoles
title: Turning succinimides and oxindoles straight into pyrroles and indoles
blurb: A ruthenium catalyst (Ru3(CO)12, as little as 0.05 mol%) paired with TMDSO strips the oxygen out of succinimides and oxindoles and aromatizes them directly to pyrroles and indoles, under mild conditions and in good to high yields. Neat because it flips the usual retrosynthesis, cyclic amides as the heteroarene precursor instead of the other way round.

original_title: Synthesis of Norbornanes via Photosensitized Strain-Release Cycloaddition of Housane
title: Bridgehead-substituted norbornanes without the Diels-Alder headache
blurb: Diels-Alder gives you norbornanes easily but not bridgehead substitution. This swaps in a photosensitized strain-release cycloaddition instead: energy transfer activates a naphthyl-substituted housane, which then adds across alkenes to install substitution patterns the classic route can't reach.

original_title: Comparative Catalytic Pyrolysis of LDPE over H-Beta and H-ZSM-5
title: H-Beta vs H-ZSM-5 for cracking LDPE at 375°C
blurb: A head-to-head of two zeolites on batch LDPE pyrolysis, with structure and acidity mapped by XRD, SEM, BET, and NH3-TPD, then product yields and liquid composition weighed against each other. Exactly the kind of catalyst screening that decides whether plastic-to-fuel pyrolysis needs to run hot or not.

original_title: How Far Does an Active Site Reach? Defining Interaction Radii in Covalent Organic Framework Electrocatalysts for Nitrate Reduction
title: Active sites aren't points, they have a reach
blurb: A perspective arguing that treating catalytic sites in COF nitrate-reduction electrocatalysts as localized points misses the length scale actually governing the multistep reaction. They propose an 'interaction radius' instead, a reframe of how selectivity in porous electrocatalysts should be explained rather than a new material.

original_title: Coordination-Sphere Control of H2 Activation and Halide-Assisted Inner-Sphere C–C Bond Formation at Formally d10 Cu(I) Centers
title: How a d10 Cu(I) center splits H2 without redox gymnastics
blurb: DFT on Cu(I)-catalyzed coupling of alkynes with allylic chlorides, run through hydride chemistry instead of the two-electron redox cycle you'd expect from a d10 metal. Ligand-assisted heterolytic H2 cleavage forms Cu-H via a reversible, uphill pre-equilibrium, which the calculations flag as the real gatekeeper for the whole C-C bond-forming pathway.

original_title: Circumventing thermodynamic limitations in converting carbon dioxide into carbon nanotubes via tandem catalysis
title: Making carbon nanotubes out of CO2 without the thermodynamics fighting back
blurb: Direct CO2-to-CNT conversion is thermodynamically uphill and usually dead-ends in amorphous soot. Pairing an electrochemical step with a thermochemical one routes around that limit to get actual nanotubes, a CO2 fix for a process that otherwise runs on fossil-fed CVD.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

original_title: Synergistic Tuning of Photoreduction Reactivity in Dihydrophenazine Photocatalysts via Fluorination and Annulative π-Extension
title: Fluorination and ring-locking, tested apart and together, on a phenazine photocatalyst
blurb: Four dihydrophenazine variants, DPZ plus fluorinated, locked, and both, let them separate what fluorination does from what molecular locking does to reactivity in a visible-light ATRC between 1,6-enynes and perfluorobutyl iodide. Locking boosts light absorption on its own; having all four side by side is what actually pins down which change is doing the work.

original_title: Ladder Acenes: Staircase-Bending Nanographenes
title: Nanographenes that bend like a staircase
blurb: Two nonplanar nanographenes, made by fusing contorted hexabenzocoronene units into an octacene (L8) and nonacene (L9) backbone, and the crystal structures confirm the staircase bend, 1.95 and 2.18 nm long with waggling peripheral rings. First molecular model of this staircase-bent acene geometry, with the broken symmetry pitched as the reason the optoelectronics get interesting.

original_title: Ruthenium-Catalyzed C–H Alkenylation of Phosphines: Reaction Development, Mechanistic Studies, and Applications to Ligand Design
title: A phosphine C-H alkenylation that builds its own ligand library
blurb: P(III)-directed Ru catalysis olefinates tertiary phosphines directly, and they used it to build 55 axially chiral olefin-phosphine ligands tolerating up to 15 functional groups. Some beat commercial biarylphosphines in Suzuki coupling at loadings down to 0.005 mol%, which is the number that gets a ligand adopted rather than filed away.

original_title: Phosphite-Mediated Peptide Bond Formation through Fragment Condensation
title: A phosphite fix for peptide fragment condensation's epimerization problem
blurb: Activating a peptide fragment's C-terminus for condensation usually risks epimerization next door via oxazolone formation. Swapping in tri(p-tolyl) phosphite as the coupling reagent heads that off, useful for anyone doing fragment condensation to build oligopeptides without racemizing the joint.

original_title: Pyridine-Boryl Radical-Mediated Dehalogenative Pyridylation Reaction for the Construction of Pyridylated Tri- and Tetrarylmethanes
title: A base that speeds up the debromination step, not just the coupling
blurb: Benzylic halides couple with 4-cyanopyridine under tBuOLi or DABCO to give diaryl- and triarylmethyl C4-pyridines with broad functional group tolerance. DFT says the base isn't just mopping up byproduct, it coordinates the pyridine-boryl radical directly and lowers the barrier for the rate-limiting debromination step.

original_title: Carbon-11 Isotopic Labeling and PET Evaluation of Serodolin: A β-Arrestin-Biased Ligand with Antinociceptive Properties
title: Watching a biased 5-HT7 painkiller candidate actually get into the brain
blurb: Serodolin, a beta-arrestin-biased 5-HT7 agonist with antinociceptive effects in animals, gets a carbon-11 label via Staudinger/aza-Wittig chemistry (a three-step azide precursor, 18% yield) so PET can confirm it crosses the blood-brain barrier and binds specifically. Still preclinical, but it's the imaging check you want before pushing a biased agonist any further.

original_title: Photocatalytic Deoxygenative Hydroalkylation Enables Modular Access to CF3-Substituted Oxetanes
title: A shortcut to CF3 oxetanes, the tert-butyl stand-ins medchem keeps wanting
blurb: Visible-light photocatalysis turns alpha-CF3 oxetane benzoates into oxetanyl radicals, with formate doing the reductive work, and adds them across plain unactivated alkenes to give CF3-oxetanes under mild conditions from simple starting material. These are catching on as tert-butyl bioisosteres but were a pain to make, so a modular route from easy precursors is the actual news.

original_title: Electroreductive N-Debenzylation of Amines and Amide Derivatives in an Undivided Cell
title: Debenzylation without the palladium or the hydrogen tank
blurb: An undivided electrochemical cell, magnesium anode, carbon-felt cathode, strips benzyl groups off amines, amides, carbamates, ureas and lactams at room temperature with no Pd and no H2. It's selective for the benzylic C-N bond and leaves carbonyls untouched, which makes it a genuinely useful late-stage deprotection option for densely functionalized molecules.

original_title: Direct Binding of Cysteine-367 Thiolate to the Active Site of the [FeFe]-Hydrogenase from Clostridium beijerinckii in the O2-Stable State
title: The cysteine that's probably why this hydrogenase doesn't die in air
blurb: CbA5H, the O2-tolerant [FeFe]-hydrogenase from Clostridium beijerinckii, survives oxygen exposure by flipping into an inactive Hinact state rather than degrading outright. This work pins down that a nearby cysteine (C367) thiolate directly binds the catalytic iron in that state, confirming the earlier ~3.1 A crystallographic hint that this is the switch protecting the active site.

original_title: Hydroxymethylation of alkynes with N-methylamines and water enabled by Co/photoredox dual catalysis
title: Turning alkynes into hydroxymethylated products with just water and an amine
blurb: Cobalt/photoredox dual catalysis hydroxymethylates alkynes, drawing on N-methylamines and water as the reagents. Not much detail to go on beyond that, but using water as part of the hydroxymethyl source is the kind of trick worth watching if it holds up across substrates.

original_title: A Heterogenized Molecular Manganese Catalyst for Aqueous CO2-to-Methanol Electroreduction in a Zero-Gap Electrolyzer
title: A molecular manganese catalyst that actually survives in a real CO2 electrolyzer
blurb: Most molecular CO2RR catalysts look great in a beaker and fall apart the moment you build a real device around them. This one, a Mn-carbonyl complex with a triazole ligand designed for heterogenization, gets built into a zero-gap aqueous electrolyzer and runs CO2 to methanol instead of stalling out at CO or formate like most of these systems do.

original_title: Gram-Scale Preparation of 4,4,4-Trifluorobut-2-ynal from HFO-1234yf
title: Making CF3-alkyne building blocks out of leftover refrigerant
blurb: A three-step, gram-scale route to 4,4,4-trifluorobut-2-ynal starting from HFO-1234yf, the cheap, widely available fourth-gen refrigerant. Trifluoropropyne, then a Bodroux-Chichibabin step to the diethoxy acetal, then hydrolysis to the aldehyde, giving more CF3-alkyne building blocks from a feedstock nobody's fighting over.

original_title: Trifluoromethylthio Engineering Enables a Balanced Electrostatic Potential for Organic Solar Cells with over 20% Efficiency and Low Energy Loss
title: SCF3 instead of CF3 pushes organic solar cells past 20%
blurb: Swapping trifluoromethylthio (SCF3) in for the usual fluorination or CF3 on a quinoxaline-core nonfullerene acceptor, plus tuned alkyl side chains, yields three new acceptors that push organic solar cells over 20% efficiency with lower nonradiative energy loss. The claim is that SCF3 balances the electrostatic potential better than plain fluorination, which is what's been capping exciton binding energy in these acceptors.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed C–H Sulfonylation with NSAPI Participation under the Assistance of Directing Group
title: Cu-catalyzed C-H sulfonylation that regenerates its own catalyst with air
blurb: Ortho C-H sulfonylation of 8-aminoquinoline-directed benzoic acids using N-sulfonyl-aminophthalimide as the sulfonyl source, running through a radical mechanism where C-H cleavage is the rate-determining step. Atmospheric oxygen reoxidizes the copper, so catalyst loading stays low and the scope stays broad without a stoichiometric oxidant.

original_title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral δ-Caprolactams: Access to a Key Intermediate of Ubrogepant
title: Building ubrogepant's chiral lactam without enzymes
blurb: Chiral δ-caprolactam is the pharmacophore in CGRP antagonists like ubrogepant and atogepant, and it's notoriously hard to make cleanly. This route builds the lactam ring in one pot, then sets all three stereocenters by crystallization-induced dynamic kinetic resolution and catalytic hydrogenation, no enzymes needed. Scalable is the pitch, and skipping biocatalysis entirely is the actual selling point here.

original_title: Lanthanum-Catalyzed Regioselective Synthesis of 1- or 4-Functionalized Dibenzofurans via Aryne Intermediates
title: Aryne chemistry picks a side on dibenzofuran substitution
blurb: Lanthanum catalysis turns halogenated arylphenols or diaryl ethers into 1- or 4-functionalized dibenzofurans, running through aryne intermediates and lithiated dibenzofuran species that get trapped by electrophiles. Dibenzofurans show up everywhere in natural products and materials, and getting to pick 1- versus 4- on purpose instead of settling for a mixture is the point.

original_title: Cycloaddition Enables Ring Opening of N -Propargyl Oxazolidines: Access to N -Benzyl-2,3-diphenylpyrroles via Both C–O and C–C Bond Cleavage
title: Snapping open an oxazolidine ring to build pyrroles
blurb: A metal- and oxidant-free cascade turns simple diphenyloxazolidines into N-benzyl-2,3-diphenylpyrroles, cleaving both a C–O and a C–C bond along the way. DMSO ends up serving as the proton source, and the mechanism runs through benzaldehyde elimination, all from easily accessible starting material rather than something prefunctionalized.

original_title: Cathodic Aziridination Using Dichloramine-T as a Nitrogen Source
title: Aziridine synthesis from the cathode side, for once
blurb: Electrochemical aziridination has always meant anodic oxidation, but this runs it in reverse, forming the ring by cathodic reduction with dichloramine-T supplying the nitrogen. They even used Gaussian process regression to pick the conditions instead of the usual grid search. Broad substrate scope, and it fills in a reductive half of electrochemical aziridine chemistry that just wasn't there.

original_title: Kinetic Resolution of α,β-Unsaturated Sulfoxides via Rh-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation
title: Sorting racemic vinyl sulfoxides by hydrogenating half of them
blurb: A Rh/(S,S)-f-spiroPhos catalyst does kinetic resolution on racemic α,β-unsaturated sulfoxides, hydrogenating one enantiomer preferentially and leaving chiral vinyl sulfoxides behind with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Works both for sulfoxides with only a sulfur stereocenter and the harder case with carbon and sulfur centers together, in the same reaction.

original_title: Organic Photoredox-Catalyzed TEMPO Disproportionation: Development of a Mild Platform for In Situ Oxoammonium Ion Formation
title: Making oxoammonium salts with light instead of acid
blurb: TEMPO normally needs a strong acid to disproportionate into the oxoammonium ion that actually does the oxidizing. This swaps that for visible light and an organic photocatalyst at under 0.1 mol%, needing only a weak acid, mild enough to leave acid-sensitive groups intact. Works across primary benzylic, allylic, and aliphatic alcohols.

original_title: Versatile Construction of a 4-Substituted Piperidine by Continuous Preparation of a Complex Grignard and Addition to an In Situ Generated Pyridinium Species
title: Outrunning an unstable Grignard with a flow reactor
blurb: Building the hindered 4-substituted piperidine core of a KRAS G12C inhibitor meant adding a bulky Grignard to an in situ pyridinium salt to forge a congested C–C bond, but the Grignard reagent degrades too fast for that to work in a normal batch process at scale. The fix is generating it continuously in a plug flow reactor and feeding it straight into the reaction, a process fix more than a new reaction.

original_title: Visible Light-Driven Water Oxidation Initiated by a Surface Bound RuIV═O Catalyst with Chloride as the Mediator
title: A surface-bound ruthenium oxo catalyst that oxidizes water with chloride's help
blurb: A photoanode built from a chromophore-catalyst assembly on SnO2/TiO2, running water oxidation in NaCl solution with a light-absorbing RuII unit feeding electrons to a RuIV=O water-oxidation catalyst, and chloride acting as the go-between. Molecular-level engineering of an artificial photosynthesis electrode, not something you're plugging into a wall yet.

original_title: Directing CO2 Hydrogenation to Light Aromatics via Molecular Traffic Control in a Dual‑Zeolite Catalyst
title: Zeolites playing traffic cop between CO2 and benzene
blurb: CO2-to-aromatics hydrogenation usually goes sideways because the intermediates wander down the wrong pathway. This trifunctional GaZnZrOx/SAPO-34/ZSM-5 catalyst boxes them in instead: CO2 to methanol on one site, then C–C coupling and aromatization handed off through a dual-zeolite structure that keeps the reaction pointed at BTX instead of letting it sprawl into byproducts.

original_title: Biocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolutions Enable Enantiodivergent Access to Axially Chiral Biaryl Dimethanols via Transient Seven-Membered Lactols
title: Enzymes now do atroposelective chemistry on biaryl alcohols too
blurb: Engineered alcohol dehydrogenases run a dynamic kinetic resolution on axially chiral biaryl dimethanols through a transient seven-membered lactol, and can be steered to either atropisomer depending on which enzyme you pick. Direct enantiodivergent routes to this compound class barely existed before, biocatalytic or otherwise, so getting there at all is the news.

original_title: Rh2(II)-Catalyzed Enyne Cycloisomerization toward 6–6–5 Tricycles
title: A dirhodium route to 6-6-5 tricycles, five stereocenters and all diastereoselective
blurb: Enynes off cyclohexadienone-tethered ynals cyclize under a dirhodium catalyst straight into 6-6-5 fused tricycles with three stereocenters set in one step, apparently through a dirhodium carbene. Trap that carbene with an external alkene instead and you get spirocyclic adducts with five stereocenters, still fully diastereoselective.

original_title: Improved cross-presentation enabled by fusion-dependent mini-proteins that efficiently reach the dendritic cell cytosol
title: Mini-proteins that actually make it into the dendritic cell cytosol
blurb: Antigens dendritic cells are supposed to cross-present to CD8+ T-cells usually get stuck in endosomes before reaching the cytosol. This uses fusion-dependent mini-proteins engineered to clear that bottleneck, with separate biophysical and cell-biology assays quantifying uptake, internalization, and display rather than just the endpoint readout. Better delivery machinery for priming T-cells against tumors and pathogens, assuming it holds up outside the assay.

original_title: Discovery of Potent and Orally Bioavailable Diaminoquinazoline-Derived mRNA Decapping Scavenger (DcpS) Enzyme Inhibitors for Treatment of Solid Tumors
title: An oral DcpS inhibitor that grabs a different pocket than the others
blurb: DcpS has mostly been chased as an AML/GBM target in FHIT-deficient cancers, not solid tumors broadly. Compound 17 engages the second nucleotide-binding domain of the mRNA cap substrate instead of the usual site and beats known inhibitors on potency in NSCLC A549 cells. Oral and aimed at solid tumors, so worth watching if that binding mode and the selectivity it implies hold up.

original_title: Progress of photothermal/thermal catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation by metal-modified CeO 2
title: A survey of CeO2 catalysts for turning CO2 back into something useful
blurb: A rundown of photothermal and plain thermal CO2 hydrogenation over noble- and non-noble-metal-modified CeO2, comparing routes to valuable chemicals rather than reporting one new result. Review territory, not a single number to hang a hook on.

original_title: High-Ratio Partial Proteolysis with Carrier Proteome (HOLSER) Enables Global Structure Profiling and Site-Resolved Elucidation of Ligand–Protein Interactions
title: More proteome coverage out of partial proteolysis, via a carrier protein trick
blurb: HOLSER pushes partial-proteolysis structure profiling further by digesting at a high enzyme ratio alongside a carrier proteome and stretching digestion time, which buys deeper, broader peptide-level coverage than these methods usually manage. The payoff is site-resolved mapping of where ligands actually touch proteins across more of the proteome at once.

original_title: A latent hydrazone switch turns SP2509 into an optical timer of cell fate
title: Turning an old LSD1 inhibitor into a light-controlled clock
blurb: SP2509 already inhibits LSD1/KDM1A reversibly, but it turns out it's carrying a latent hydrazone switch nobody was using: 430 nm light flips it into a less-active cis state, and it relaxes back to the more active trans form in the dark with a 6.5-hour half-life. That's a built-in timer for dosing chromatin state on a schedule instead of just picking a concentration.

original_title: Computational Insights into BF3-Catalyzed [2π + 2σ] Cycloadditions: Catalyst, Substrate, Solvent, and Electric Field Effects
title: Why BF3 only ever gives one regiochemistry in this bicyclobutane cycloaddition
blurb: DFT and DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS on the BF3-catalyzed [2π+2σ] cycloaddition between dihydropyridines and bicyclobutanes, chasing why the reaction sticks to the azacycle-fused product, bond forming next to the DHP nitrogen, and never touches the alternative at the remote double bond. The targets are azacycle-fused bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, benzene bioisosteres medicinal chemists already reach for, so this is mechanistic backfill for a reaction people use, not a new one.

original_title: Metallo-Organic Tetrahedral Cages with Aggregation-Induced Emission for High-Efficiency White Light-Emitting Diodes
title: Rigid metal-organic cages that glow yellow alone, white with a dash of blue
blurb: Two tetrahedral cages, C1 and C2, get aggregation-induced emission from being too rigid to shed energy non-radiatively. Solvent-controlled aggregation pushes fluorescence quantum yields to 26% and 45% with yellow emission near 550-600 nm, and just dropping a blue emitter (DMA) into the solution shifts the output to white light. Reads like a step toward solution-processable white LEDs, though it's still cage chemistry in a cuvette.

original_title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Shows Efficacy for Pediatric Sarcoma - Labroots
title: An ADC posts results in pediatric sarcoma
blurb: Efficacy data for an antibody-drug conjugate in pediatric sarcoma, a space that's short on options beyond chemo. Nothing beyond that here.

original_title: Design Rules for Tuning Thermal Lifetimes of Arylazopyrazole Photoswitches
title: Mapping 30,000 azo-photoswitches to learn what sets their clock speed
blurb: Arylazopyrazole photoswitches flip nearly quantitatively under light, but their thermal half-lives swing wildly by substituent with no clean rule for predicting which. This trains a machine-learned interatomic potential on DFT data and uses it to scan isomerization pathways, adiabatic and nonadiabatic, across close to 30,000 derivatives at once. A design map for tuning thermal lifetimes rather than one new switch.

original_title: Enantioselective hydrogenation of hydroxyacetone on intrinsically chiral Pt(643) surfaces
title: Chiral platinum surfaces try to replace the homogeneous catalyst
blurb: DFT and microkinetic modeling test intrinsically chiral Pt(643) surfaces for hydrogenating hydroxyacetone to 1,2-propanediol, a heterogeneous stand-in for the molecular chiral catalysts that dominate this chemistry but complicate separation and recycling. It's all computation so far, no measured ee yet.

original_title: Synthesis of Benzofurans and Dihydrobenzofurans from Phenols: Diastereoselective Benzylic C–H and Phenolic Site Annulation with Nsp 3 -ylides
title: Ylides that build benzofurans instead of rearranging
blurb: Nitrile-stabilized ammonium ylides annulate phenols at the benzylic C-H and the phenolic oxygen, giving benzofurans and dihydrobenzofuran-2-carbonitriles with diastereoselective control of the new chiral center. The interesting part is mechanistic: these ylides act as arylmethylene transfer synthons here rather than running their usual sigmatropic rearrangements, and they're reported to outreact sulfoxonium and pyridinium ylides.

original_title: I2–DMSO-Mediated In Situ Capture of Ketenimine Cations by Two Molecules of 3-Aminoindazole for the Synthesis of 1-(1 H -Indazol-3-yl)-2,4-Diphenyl-1 H -Pyrrolo[2′,3′:4,5]Pyrimido[1,2- b ]Indazole Derivatives
title: One pot, two aminoindazoles, one very long heterocycle
blurb: An I2-DMSO system traps an in situ ketenimine cation with two equivalents of 3-aminoindazole, building a pyrrolo-pyrimido-indazole scaffold in one pot from aminoindazoles, acetophenones, and enaminones. Structure confirmed by X-ray, and the scope runs to 40 compounds, some flagged for their UV absorption. A methodology paper with no stated application yet.

original_title: France: Curium to merge with Lantheus in mega US$8bn radiopharmaceutical transaction - Investors in Healthcare
title: Curium and Lantheus are merging into one $8bn radiopharma company
blurb: France's Curium is combining with Lantheus in an $8bn deal, consolidating two of the bigger names in radiopharmaceuticals into one. The interesting question is what happens to overlapping pipeline programs once they're under the same roof.

original_title: Harnessing Triplets of TIPS-Anthracene-Based Au(I) Complexes for Photoinduced Electron Transfer and Room-Temperature Phosphorescence
title: Gold on a TIPS-anthracene, watching what it does to the triplet
blurb: Two new Au(I) complexes, a monomer and a dimer, built from a diphenylphosphine-TIPS-anthracene ligand, probing photoinduced electron transfer and room-temperature phosphorescence in a triplet-mediated acene system. Metal-functionalized acenes are rare enough that the excited-state characterization is itself the result here, not a step toward some device.

original_title: Data-Guided Discovery of Cu-Host Single-Atom Alloys for Selective Electrohydrogenation via Intermediate Hydrogen Binding
title: ML picks the Cu alloy that hydrogenates without just making H2
blurb: A DFT dataset of surface H* binding energies trains an interpretable machine-learning model to find Cu-based single-atom alloys sitting in an intermediate H* binding regime, strong enough to supply hydrogen for electrocatalytic upgrading of biomass oxygenates, weak enough to not lose it all to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Data-guided catalyst design aimed squarely at a real selectivity problem in electrifying biomass chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Lattice Strain-Induced d-p Orbital Hybridization Stabilizes Frustrated Lewis Pairs for Ultra-Stable CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
title: Straining a frustrated Lewis pair so it survives CO2-to-methanol heat
blurb: Zr-doping a ceria surface induces lattice strain that reshuffles Ce 5d-O 2p orbital hybridization, stabilizing the surface hydroxyls that make up the frustrated Lewis pair for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. FLPs are good at activating CO2 but usually too thermally fragile for real operating temperatures, and this is a defect-engineering fix rather than a new catalyst class.

original_title: Spectacular - A Modular DAQ System for Microdosimetry
title: A DAQ system built for microdosimetry's tiny signals
blurb: Spectacular is a modular data-acquisition system for microdosimetry in particle therapy with protons, helium, and carbon ions, measuring energy deposition at the micrometer scale needed to get linear energy transfer alongside absorbed dose. Instrumentation aimed at the small-signal problem that's apparently been holding this measurement back.

original_title: Gem-Dimethyl Selenoketal: Suppressing Sulfur–Selenium Exchange with Antioxidant and Anti-Inflammatory Activities
title: A selenoketal that stops trading itself for sulfur
blurb: Organoselenium antioxidants tend to react promiscuously with biological thiols, scrambling into off-target selenium-sulfur exchange that causes toxicity. This diselenium ketal diamine adds a gem-dimethyl group from acetone condensation to block that exchange, keeping the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity intact. A stability fix at the molecular level rather than a new mechanism.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Discovery of Deuterated 3,4-Dihydro-benzo[ e ][1,4]diazepine-2,5-dione Derivatives as Potent, Selective and Orally Bioavailable ROCK2 Inhibitors
title: Deuterating a ROCK2 inhibitor to fix its pharmacokinetics
blurb: SAR on a series of 1-methyl-dihydrobenzodiazepine-diones as selective ROCK2 inhibitors for metastatic breast cancer, with deuterium swapped in at specific positions purely to improve the pharmacokinetic profile. The lead, compound 22d, comes out potent, selective, and orally bioavailable, with deuterium doing a supporting role rather than being the point of the paper.

original_title: Improved Library of Pyrrolidine-2,3-dione Monomers as Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Agents against Staphylococcus aureus
title: A CF3 group is what's making these S. aureus killers better
blurb: A new generation of pyrrolidine-2,3-dione monomers, built via a multicomponent reaction, going after both S. aureus itself and the biofilms it hides in. The upgrade over earlier generations comes down to one change, a para-trifluoromethyl on the N-aryl substituent.

original_title: Trapping the Excess Electron of FeB-Type CeSi by Hydrogenation ─ Formation of Ferromagnetic Hydrides CeSiH x ( T C ≈ 24 K)
title: Hydrogen turns FeB-type CeSi into a magnet
blurb: Hydrogenating CeSi gives two distinct hydrides, a kinetic phase that keeps the original FeB structure and a thermodynamically favored one that flips to CrB-type. Both order ferromagnetically, with Curie temperatures around 22 to 24 K, unusually high for a cerium intermetallic.

original_title: From Caffeine to Aspirin: Everyday Molecules as Triggers for Genetically Encoded Proximity Systems
title: Caffeine and aspirin as the on-switch for engineered cells
blurb: Chemically induced proximity systems usually run on synthetic ligands with real baggage, off-target effects, immunogenicity, dosing limits. This perspective rounds up CIP platforms triggered instead by dietary molecules and OTC drugs, the pitch being that reusing compounds already cleared for humans skips a lot of the translational headache.

original_title: Logic-Gated Dual-Aptamer Proximity AlphaLISA for Rapid and Sensitive Detection of Tumor-Derived Small Extracellular Vesicles
title: This assay only lights up if two aptamers agree
blurb: A logic-gated AlphaLISA where EpCAM and PD-L1 aptamers both have to land on the same vesicle to bring the donor and acceptor beads close enough to signal. Wash-free, and aimed at the single-marker specificity problem that makes tumor-derived sEV detection so messy.

original_title: Probing Nanoscale Features of Electrospun Amorphous Solid Dispersions Using Advanced Biophysical Analysis
title: Catching aspirin crystallize out of its polymer, with neutrons
blurb: Small-angle neutron scattering used to catch the nanoscale, early-stage recrystallization in electrospun amorphous solid dispersions, aspirin standing in as the model drug. Most methods only see instability once it's already wrecked the formulation, this one's pointed at the onset.

original_title: Development of the DUMBO imaging device for beta-emitting radionuclides within the ISOLPHARM collaboration
title: A new imaging rig for beta-emitting isotopes
blurb: DUMBO, an imaging device developed under the ISOLPHARM collaboration for beta-emitting radionuclides. Light on details beyond that, but a piece of kit worth knowing about if you work with these isotopes.

original_title: A concentration-independent paradigm rendering weak interactions inherently quantifiable
title: Weak binding doesn't have to hide behind concentration anymore
blurb: Millimolar-affinity interactions run a lot of cell biology but have resisted quantification because biochemistry has always read binding through bulk concentration, cranking molecule number while holding volume fixed, until you run out of practical concentration to crank. This reframes the measurement so those weak interactions become quantifiable without hitting that wall.

original_title: Curium Announces Definitive Agreement to Merge with Lantheus - GlobeNewswire
title: Curium and Lantheus are becoming one company
blurb: A definitive agreement to merge, announced straight off the wire. The deal is official, terms aren't in this announcement.

original_title: Unveiling Temperature-Dependent Ligand Gating in Atomically Precise Pd4S Catalysts for Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
title: Pd4S clusters that open and close their ligands with heat
blurb: An atomically precise, sulfur-stabilized [Pd4S(dtbbpy)4(μ-CO)2]2+ nanocluster, made by slow-releasing the sulfur source instead of dumping it in all at once. Stable enough to actually study as a model catalyst, and its ligand behavior gates with temperature to control selectivity in alkyne hydrogenation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: [OC] In Silico directed evolution of enzyme I made for a class I audiy
title: [OC] In Silico directed evolution of enzyme I made for a class I audiy
blurb: I created this directed evolution pipeline to improve an enzyme that breaks 1-fluorodecane, for a biochem course I audited enjoy!
